# Turn a settings file into a runnable session

[A configuration file should describe a computation, and the resulting computation should have an answer you can check.]{.lesson-deck}
:::

The old `json_read` program printed raw JSON. This version uses the native
settings loader and constructs a real spectral CPU session. JSON and TOML
describe the same domain, method, backend and time interval. Physics
remains a small visible callback.

## Load the native schema

```{.cpp include="model.cpp" snippet="session" dedent=4}
```

`load_settings_file` recognizes `.json` and `.toml` and reports syntax
errors. `make_simulation_session` interprets the domain and time schema
and checks that method/backend selection matches the requested stack.
Choosing `"method":"fd"` cannot silently turn a `SpectralCPUStack`
into a finite-difference stack.

The domain uses `size`, `lower` and `upper`. On the periodic x axis,
$h_x=(\mathrm{upper}_x-\mathrm{lower}_x)/N_x$; the upper boundary is not
a duplicated sample. The default interval $[-2,6)$ therefore has length 8.

## Let the session own the clock and stack

For $u_t=\Delta u$, start with
$u(x,0)=1+.2\cos[2\pi(x+2)/8]$ and apply backward Euler in Fourier space:

```{.cpp include="model.cpp" snippet="run" dedent=4}
```

The callback receives the actual accepted interval. The default steps are
.07, .07 and .06, ending at .2. A multiplier cached once for .07 would
integrate the wrong final interval. The mean stays one and the mode's
amplitude is multiplied by $\prod_m(1+k^2\Delta t_m)^{-1}$, where
$k=2\pi/8$.

## Compare the two file formats

```sh
openpfc run model.cpp input.json --launcher=none
```

The companion [TOML file](input.toml) describes the same computation.
After building OpenPFC, run it from the repository root with:

```sh
./builds/release/examples/json_read examples/configuration/session/input.toml
```

Adjust `builds/release` to your build directory. The numerical regression
launches the built executable with each file and checks identical complete
fields and equivalent normalized settings. Source-based `openpfc run`
currently validates JSON when snapshotting its input; TOML is supported
by the library loader used by the compiled program.

Rank zero writes the parsed document to `results/settings.json`; every
rank writes its owned values to `results/field_rank_*.csv`.
There is no interactive stdin prompt. Change the bounds, timestep or
backend token, then inspect either the result or the native validation
message. This lesson demonstrates session construction, not every
application-specific `model.params` schema.

Keep the [source](model.cpp), [JSON input](input.json) and
[TOML input](input.toml) together. Continue with
[time-loop hooks](../../heat/driver-hooks/index.qmd) or
writing a result series.
